description: What this runtime sent to one counterpart and what came back, as hashes and shapes, never content. For each message sent: the address, seq and sha256 the service stored, or over a transport its mark, via and the sha256 of the envelope it carried, whether it was sealed and how long it was, seen_by_them when a signed message from them names that sha256 as read and opened, and answered_by_them when one answers it. A claim covers the one message it names: a message nothing names is listed in no_read_claim and is unknown, not unread. For each message received: whether it opened, which fields it had, and which of yours it answers (re) or names as read (seen). Use it when a partner says a message did not arrive or arrived empty: the sha256 is of the bytes that went, what the service stored or the envelope a transport carried, byte for byte, and theirs should match. Every message this runtime sends is sealed to the recipient's key, so a reader without that key sees an envelope and no text, apart from one sent readable and one over a transport under a readable profile, which are signed and not sealed. The one over a transport is listed here with sealed false. The one sent readable goes to an address with no known key and has no line here, since the trace follows a counterpart's key: keep the sha256 its send answer gave, and read no_trace as nothing recorded, not as nothing sent. Without who, one line per counterpart.

limit.description: messages each way, newest last; 20 by default

who.description: a partner name, a key or a write address; leave out for everyone

name: aamio_trace
